svg.text: Print shop sheet: Nimbus case
Bring this page and the three STL files in the pack folder.
What to ask for
Three parts, printed once each: front_shell.stl, back_cover.stl, ground_inlay.stl.
Material: PLA, matte if they have it, cream or off-white (#EFEBE4). The small inlay in terracotta (#B5502C).
Layer height 0.2 mm, 6 wall lines (2.4 mm), 15 percent gyroid infill, no supports, no raft.
Orientation is already set in the STL files: front shell face down, back cover back down.
Biggest part 236 x 228 x 86 mm: needs a bed of 256 x 256 mm or more (Bambu class).
Both shells measure about 236 x 228 mm, so they print whole on a 256 x 256 mm bed. A smaller bed does not fit them.
Check before you pay
The two shells should sit together with a thin even gap. Do a dry fit with the panel and the Pi before gluing.
Do not scale the files. Units are millimetres. Tolerance about 0.3 mm.
Rough size of the job (estimates, not quotes)
Model volume 378 cm3, filament about 470 g, machine time about 12 hours.
Material: about 15 to 25 dollars of filament. A shop will often charge 60 to 200 dollars for this much machine time.
Those money and time numbers are estimates from the mesh volume and typical rates, not from a quote.
You also need to buy
See bom.csv: a Pi 4, a 16:9 panel, two USB-C extenders, a jack, an SD extender, a few screws and tape.
Files
front_shell.stl, back_cover.stl, ground_inlay.stl, nimbus-blueprint-1to1-A3.pdf, bom.csv, print-sheet.csv.
Exact CAD in the .step files. Drawn from the CAD by docs/hardware/nimbus_pack.py.
